g.textArea: People will buy it because cardiology guidelines need which relative and what age, intake forms take it from memory, and for $500 per cardiologist a year a practice-sent link puts those details, sourced, in the chart before visit one.

We can make it because the patient side already runs on open health standards, a PDF reaches any chart, and a pilot on vendors that sign HIPAA contracts costs under $850 a month, which 17–21 paying cardiologists cover, founders unpaid.

Word for word as on the slide 9 cards of the Maker Day 2 deck (final, Oct 12, 2026). "Take it from memory" means: the form asks yes or no per relative, then leaves a few lines for details, with no side of family and no room for "not sure" [S5].

textArea.b: "cardiology guidelines need which relative and what age"

g.textArea: Premature heart disease counts in a parent or sibling, men < 55, women < 65 [76][74]; sudden-death, cardiomyopathy and aortic rules depend on degree and age [78][80][81]; three-generation history is the HCM standard [72]
Shown (guideline text)

[S5] asks "Heart Disease?" per relative, then free-text type and age of onset; no side of family, no "not sure"; charts still name relative and age in about 11% of positive entries [89]. EHR check-ins can show family-history questions too [S52]
Shown for one health-system form (2016 version); independent practices' forms and EHR check-ins not yet collected (test 7)
The one public per-clinician price for a family-tree tool: FamGenix, $500 a year [111]. Saved staff time only breaks even at that price (Step 4.3)
Price anchor shown; payment untested (0 of 21 interviews were practice managers; test 1)

64.2% engaged and 57% of invited finished when clinics sent a link with reminders [92]; 7.8% when the invite came as a research study needing consent [91]. Relatives' own answers are untested: 29% invite drop-off in a similar app [93]
Shown elsewhere for patients; not yet in a US cardiology practice. Relatives: untested (pilot target ≥ 25% of patients get one relative's answer)
Every fact stores who said it and when; built and tested [S28]
Built (synthetic data)
33-day average cardiology wait [S2]; eCheck-In opens up to 7 days before [S4]; more family history reached charts with a questionnaire plus EHR upload [S10]; ID007 (note)
Timing shown; filing at one practice still to test

textArea.b: "the patient side already runs on open health standards"

g.textArea: SMART on FHIR launch, FHIR export, live routes, tests [S28]
Shown (synthetic data); the pilot backend is not built yet (Step 5.1)
PDF works with every practice, by link, fax or upload; staff may still re-key [research §1.7]
Shown in principle; test at one practice

textArea.b: "a pilot on vendors that sign HIPAA contracts costs under $850 a month, which 17–21 paying cardiologists cover, founders unpaid"

g.textArea: $689–834 a month under BAAs (Step 5.3); 17–21 paying cardiologists at $500 per cardiologist per year (9–11 groups of two)
Shown from price pages; insurance is an estimate; founder support time not counted
